# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Mortgage, Housing, KiwiSaver, Income & Protection Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset and data dictionary built 100% live from official New Zealand Crown and statutory releases, with clearly labelled HLF-derived calculations and interpretation.
> Created by: Andy Palliser (Andrew Jonathan Palliser, FSP1004725), Mortgage & KiwiSaver Adviser · Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/team/andrew-palliser) | Published by: Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/).
> Media Kit & Citation Guide: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations | HLF Glossary: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/tools/glossary
> Reuse Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) for HLF-derived figures & commentary; official statistics credited to their respective publishers.
> Date Standard: Observation Period (latest monthly: Latest Official Release) | Period End | Source Publication Date | Last Checked (16 November 2026 / 2026-11-16).
> Active datasets: 33.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Data Dictionary & Reality Check Benchmarks (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/
- Media Kit & Citation Guide (HTML): https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations

## Canonical Data Dictionary Records (33 Active Datasets)
- [Annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home (CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after reference quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, the cost of purchasing a newly built home changed by +3.2% year-on-year, compared with 3.7% headline CPI inflation. [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Purchase of newly built home = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Directly reported Stats NZ CPI purchase of new housing = +3.2% YoY | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Annual change in the cost of purchasing a newly built home (CPI)," September 2026 quarter. Source: Stats NZ — Consumers Price Index (Purchase of new housing sub-index). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/build-cost-inflation/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Annual residential dwelling (building) insurance price index inflation (Stats NZ CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after reference quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/building-insurance-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, residential dwelling (building) insurance prices changed by +1.2% year-on-year—sitting -2.5 percentage points relative to headline CPI inflation (+3.7%). [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Dwelling insurance price index = +1.2% YoY; All-groups CPI = +3.7% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Dwelling insurance CPI (+1.2%) minus All-groups CPI (+3.7%) = -2.5 percentage points | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Annual residential dwelling (building) insurance price index inflation (Stats NZ CPI)," September 2026 quarter. Source: Stats NZ — Consumers Price Index (Dwelling insurance sub-index). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/building-insurance-inflation/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Personal & consumer loan borrower stress: non-performing consumer loans & NPL ratio (RBNZ Table S50) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-loan-stress-npl/): In September 2026, New Zealand bank non-performing personal and consumer loans (90+ days past due or impaired) stood at 0.90% ($66m) (down from 1.1% a year earlier). [Official Data: RBNZ Table S50 (September 2026): Bank non-performing consumer loans = $66m (0.90% of consumer lending). | HLF Calculation: Non-Performing Bank Consumer Loans = $66m (0.90% of consumer loan book; vs 1.10% a year earlier) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Personal & consumer loan borrower stress: non-performing consumer loans & NPL ratio (RBNZ Table S50)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Banks: Assets – Loans by asset quality (Table S50). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-loan-stress-npl/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Total New Zealand personal & consumer lending stock across banks & non-bank lenders (RBNZ Table C5) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-personal-lending-stock/): As at September 2026, total New Zealand personal and consumer lending (personal loans, vehicle finance, hire purchase, overdrafts, and cards) stood at $14.64B ($14,636m) (up 2.2% year-on-year from $14.32B a year earlier), including $7.33B (50.1%) from non-bank lenders. [Official Data: RBNZ Table C5 (September 2026): Total consumer sector lending stock = $14,636m ($14.64B). | HLF Calculation: Total NZ Consumer Lending = $14,636m ($14.64B; YoY: +2.2%) | Non-Bank Share: $7,332m ÷ $14,636m = 50.1% | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Total New Zealand personal & consumer lending stock across banks & non-bank lenders (RBNZ Table C5)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Registered banks and non-bank lending institutions: Sector lending (Table C5). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/consumer-personal-lending-stock/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]

[Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Contents insurance price index = -0.6% YoY; All-groups CPI = +3.7% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Contents insurance CPI (-0.6%) minus All-groups CPI (+3.7%) = -4.3 percentage points | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Median equivalised household disposable income before & after housing costs (Stats NZ HILS) (Obs: Year ended June 2025 | End: 2025-06-30 | Published: Annual Stats NZ Household Income and Housing-Cost Statistics release)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/equivalised-household-income-family-size/): In the year ended june 2025, New Zealand's median equivalised household disposable income was $60,521 before housing costs and $45,645 after deducting housing costs—meaning housing outgoings absorbed 24.6% ($14,876/year per equivalised adult) of disposable income. [Official Data: Stats NZ HILS (Year ended June 2025): Median equivalised disposable income BHC = $60,521; AHC = $45,645. | HLF Calculation: Median Equivalised Disposable Income: $60,521 Before Housing Costs (BHC) vs $45,645 After Housing Costs (AHC; 24.6% housing deduction) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Inland Revenue overdue tax, entitlement & student loan debt stress (IRD) (Obs: June 2026 | End: 2026-06-30 | Published: Inland Revenue Tax and Entitlements Debt Statistics release)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/ird-overdue-tax-debt-stress/): As at June 2026, 524,000 customers held overdue tax and entitlements debt with Inland Revenue totalling $9.7B (up 4.3% year-on-year from $9.3B across 527,000 customers in June 2025—averaging $18,511 per customer in debt), including $3.2B owed by individuals (up from $3.1B). "Inland Revenue overdue tax, entitlement & student loan debt stress (IRD)," June 2026. Over the rolling 12-month period, Kāinga Ora recorded 9,556 approvals and 4,049 settled First Home Loans. [Official Data: Kāinga Ora Home Ownership Products Report (Apr - Jun 2026): First Home Loan approvals = 2,444 (686, 884, 874); settlements = 1,016 (322, 245, 449). | HLF Calculation: Quarterly Approvals: 686 + 884 + 874 = 2,444 (815/mth) | Quarterly Settlements: 322 + 245 + 449 = 1,016 (339/mth; 41.6% conversion) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. [Official Data: Kāinga Ora Home Ownership Products Report (Apr - Jun 2026 TLA Tables): Auckland City = 657 approvals (277 settlements); Christchurch City = 399 (138); Hamilton City = 170 (61). | HLF Calculation: Auckland City: 657÷2,444=26.9% | Christchurch City: 399÷2,444=16.3% | Hamilton City: 170÷2,444=7.0% | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory.
